data.narrative:
Axial Composites is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Giuseppe Rapisarda and Rollo Tully that has raised $1M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 8 private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics) plus 1 public comparable.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and serves as the primary valuation anchor. Using total raised ($1M) as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields $2.5M. Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable due to insufficient data density; the broader Robotics & Manufacturing peer set lacks sufficient same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier matches (minimum 3 required; 0 identified in the narrow filters). Relying on all-sector medians would introduce undue noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $2.125M–$2.875M, with a median implied value of $2.5M. This single-method triangulation carries material uncertainty: the lack of tight peer comparables in the immediate competitive tier limits cross-validation. Stage-progression relies on historical multiplier assumptions that may not hold for this specific market segment. Key risks to valuation include team execution, product-market fit, and capital efficiency relative to peer benchmarks. A fuller range would benefit from additional same-stage robotics company data or customer traction metrics as the company progresses.
